steps.text: /llms.txt follows the llms.txt convention
summarizes who Ian is and links to the Markdown version of every page

nodes.title: A Markdown version of every page

steps.text: every page has a Markdown version at the same path ending in .md
it's generated from the same content collections as the page

lint fails on either, naming the file and line
every component renders into a shadow root
exposes its main elements as named CSS parts listed in its docs
a plain HTML page that loads the component bundle with one script tag
every component renders and works on that page

nodes.title: Pages download only what they use

steps.text: a page that uses two components loads code for those two and the runtime, and no others
text a component shows is passed in through slots or attributes

the generated docs JSON lists all of them

nodes.title: Events are namespaced and cross the shadow boundary

they bubble and are composed

responds to Enter and Space the way its native equivalent does
every story of every component passes axe with no violations in light and in dark
a visitor prefers reduced motion
no component animates
I run "bun run gate"
every check that CI runs, runs locally in the same order
it exits non-zero, naming each check that failed

nodes.title: Every pull request runs the gate

steps.text: a pull request is opened or updated

GitHub Actions runs each check as its own required status check: typecheck, lint, format, unit and scenario tests, spec check, build, Storybook tests, end-to-end and accessibility tests, budgets and the secret scan

nodes.title: main only changes through a green, approved pull request

steps.text: main rejects direct pushes and force pushes
a pull request can't merge until every required check passes
these rules apply to admins too, so nobody can merge red
a pull request can't merge without an approving review, and a push after the approval needs a new one
only admins can skip the approval, and only when merging a pull request
"bun run gate:protection" fails if GitHub's branch protection settings don't say so
every package typechecks in strict mode
each error is reported with its file and line
ESLint, Stylelint and Prettier report no errors in any package
a file that isn't formatted fails, named

nodes.title: The design rules are lint rules

steps.text: raw colors, and primitive tokens used outside packages/tokens, fail lint in components and the site
a component tag without the kan- prefix fails lint
each failure names the rule and how to fix it

nodes.title: Behaviors are tests, and coverage never drops

steps.text: every active behavior runs as a scenario test, and one without step definitions shows as todo
a pull request fails if it turns a behavior that passes on main into todo or failing
a pull request fails if it adds .skip or .only to a test
if it adds a lint-disable, @ts-ignore or @ts-expect-error comment without a reason on the same line

nodes.title: Changes to the gates are flagged for Ian's review

steps.text: a pull request changes workflows, lint or format configs, tsconfig, budgets, thresholds or gate scripts
the protected-paths check lists those files for a close review
the pull request can't merge without Ian's approval

nodes.title: Changes to the specs are flagged for Ian's review

steps.text: a pull request changes anything under specs/
the protected-paths check lists those files for a close review
the pull request can't merge without Ian's approval
a pull request names the behavior IDs it implements in its description
the gate fails if it names none, unless it is labeled chore, or if a named ID doesn't exist
the gate lists any named behavior whose scenario still doesn't pass
each failed check reports the file, line, rule and a one-line fix
the pull request has one summary comment listing every failure, updated on every push

nodes.title: An agent can't stop on red

steps.text: a Claude Code session that changed code
the agent tries to finish while "bun run gate" fails
a Stop hook keeps it working, up to 3 attempts, and then hands over to Ian with the failures listed
AGENTS.md states the same rule for Cursor, Grok Build and any other agent
an agent's work is done only when its pull request passes every required check
the agent reports the pull request link and its check status
Ian approves and merges, and agents never merge
the full CI gate finishes in under 10 minutes
a pull request that adds a secret, key or token fails the secret scan, naming the file and line
a pull request that adds a dependency fails unless its description gives a reason for each one

nodes.title: Agents work as their own GitHub identity

steps.text: agents push branches, commit and open pull requests through the agent commands
they act as ians-agent[bot], with a token that expires within an hour
the app has no Administration or Workflows permission, so it can't change rulesets, branch protection or CI
the agent commands refuse to merge, label, push to main or force push, and Claude Code permission rules make agents use them
AGENTS.md states the same limits for Cursor, Grok Build and any other agent
the pull request template has sections for the summary, behaviors, review guide, verification, notes and dependencies
the pr-trace check fails if the summary, review guide or verification is empty, naming each one

nodes.title: The facts in a pull request are generated

steps.text: an agent runs "bun run pr:body"
it drafts the description with the behaviors that are new or changed and what they serve, the files to review closely, the added dependencies, and the gate and coverage results
it leaves the summary, review guide and notes for the agent to write

journeys live in specs/portfolio/journeys, one Markdown file each with YAML front matter
behaviors are Gherkin scenarios in specs/portfolio/features
intents are INT-NNN, journeys are JRN-NNN and behaviors are AREA-NNN
every ID is unique across the whole graph
each behavior has exactly one ID tag, whose area matches its feature's @area- tag
each journey lists the intents it serves and each of its steps lists the behaviors it relies on
intents and behaviors don't list their own edges, so there is one source of truth
every active intent is served by at least one active journey
every active journey serves at least one intent and every step names at least one behavior
every active behavior is named by at least one journey step
a journey names an intent or behavior ID that doesn't exist or is retired
the specs are checked
the check fails, naming the journey file and the bad ID
a feature file with invalid Gherkin
the specs are checked
the check fails, naming the file and line
I run "bun run specs:graph"
GRAPH.md is written with a Mermaid diagram of intents and journeys and, per journey, its steps and behaviors
graph.json is written with every node and edge for agents to read
the spec check fails when either is out of date
I run "bun run specs:trace" with an intent, journey or behavior ID
it prints the intents above it and the journeys and behaviors around it, each with its title and file location
for a behavior, the other behaviors that share its journey steps
I run "bun run specs:find" with a few words
it lists the intents, journeys and behaviors whose text matches, best match first, with their IDs
a dropped intent or journey is marked status: retired and a dropped behavior is tagged @retired
retired nodes stay in the files, keep their IDs, and are left out of the coverage checks
no ID is ever reused

nodes.title: Tokens are written in DTCG format

steps.text: every file under packages/tokens/src/primitive is valid W3C DTCG JSON
every token has a $value and a $type, on itself or inherited from its group
every primitive color is authored in the OKLCH color space
is output as an oklch() CSS value
each step is darker than the one before it
500 is the reference electric cyan the identity is built on

nodes.title: A neutral ramp tinted toward the brand

steps.text: color.neutral has the same 11 steps as color.cyan, each darker than the one before
its hue leans toward cyan with low chroma, so grays read as cool rather than flat
color.white and color.black exist on their own

nodes.title: Status ramps that can't be mistaken for the accent

steps.text: color.green, color.amber and color.red each have the same 11 steps
each of their 500 steps is at least 30 degrees of hue away from cyan 500
each step is that many multiples of 4px
font.family.mono is JetBrains Mono and font.family.sans is Inter
each ends with a system fallback stack of the same kind
font.size has steps xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl, 4xl and 5xl
md is 16px and the steps from md upward follow a 1.25 ratio, rounded to whole pixels
font.weight has regular 400, medium 500 and bold 700
font.line-height has tight 1.15, normal 1.5 and relaxed 1.7

nodes.title: Shape: small radii and thin borders

steps.text: radius has none 0, sm 2px, md 4px, lg 8px and full 9999px
border.width has thin 1px and thick 2px
duration has fast 120ms, normal 200ms and slow 320ms
easing has standard and emphasized cubic-bezier curves
breakpoint has sm 640px, md 768px, lg 1024px and xl 1280px
the home page scores at least 95 in performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO on Lighthouse mobile
CI fails a pull request that drops any score below that

no semantic token holds a raw value

nodes.title: Light and dark define the same tokens

steps.text: the semantic color tokens live in semantic/light.json and semantic/dark.json
both files define exactly the same token names
the build fails naming any token that is in one but not the other

text.on-accent reaches 4.5:1 against accent.default
each status fg reaches 4.5:1 against its status bg
